source: Robert's direct dashboard walkthrough feedback, 18 October 2026
status: Recorded for after the walkthrough. No implementation or acceptance claim.

welcomeBeforeDashboard.request: A separate welcome/next-steps landing page after initial company introduction. Do not land a new company straight in the live-customer pipeline dashboard.
tiles: Build case studies and bring in the contractor's benchmarks
Set proposal defaults/outcomes: appearance, programme or schedule presentation, suitable standard terms and conditions
welcomeBeforeDashboard.intent: Help establish company identity and intended proposal outcomes before producing a proposal. Keep the dashboard for ongoing operational work once the company is set up.
welcomeBeforeDashboard.bounds: Do not silently invent a mandatory completion gate requiring all four tiles, new financial/legal defaults, schema or provider authority. Exact defaults and welcome/resume routing need a source-grounded implementation slice after release. Existing readiness page overlaps this direction but does not implement the requested four-tile structure, especially proposal defaults/benchmarks.

brandAndVisuals: Dashboard wordmark has a different typeface/colour treatment from approved account/setup branding. Use one consistent Constructa identity, without the trailing dot already requested elsewhere.
Dashboard palette is too loud and messy: black blocks over green plus blue, purple, orange, red and bright greens. Align with restrained charcoal/green onboarding palette and cleaner surfaces.
General dashboard and Kanban layout need simplification, better hierarchy and less visual clutter.
positiveElements: Week/month/quarter/year range controls are useful, provided actual project metrics genuinely recalculate with the selected range.
Lead/opportunity capture, pipeline and operational metrics are useful core capabilities; the objection is flow, clarity and presentation, not their wholesale removal.
filtersAndStages: Pipeline/Lead/Estimating/Proposal Sent/Active/Completed/Lost row looks like buttons or filters but its purpose is unclear.

Consider a Dashboard sidebar section with expandable filters, consistent with the existing navigation pattern, rather than scattered controls. This is a design suggestion, not a selected navigation or state policy.
Card stage dropdowns and progression controls are clunky and unclear about what happens when selected. Make filtering versus changing a job's stage unambiguous.

Clarify that current pipeline cards represent jobs/opportunities rather than silently treating a customer as moving through every job stage. Do not change the domain/status model without an explicit bounded specification.
Use more engaging but clear, professional opportunity language instead of vanilla Leads wording; no final replacement labels chosen.
resourcesAndFinance: Bottom Resource Management and Financial Dashboard areas feel detached/blank. Integrate useful operational information more purposefully when functional. Current UI calls these future features; do not fabricate metrics or imply presentation closes those functional gaps.
nextWalkthroughStop: Show existing company-start/readiness page for comparison, explicitly not the newly requested design. Continue record-only; no code/tests/diagnostics or provider operations.
